articles.title: Philips OneBlade vs Standard Razors: A Worthwhile Upgrade?
articles.summary: If there’s one part of consumer technology that’s seen pretty understated leaps in the last few decades, it’s personal grooming. Whether it’s trimming your beard and trying not to remove a layer of your skin in doing so, or somewhere even more personal, the time of the manual razor is over.
body: While a good, old-fashioned razor might seem like an obvious way to trim away your five-o’clock shadow or touch up your facial hair, it’s not exactly something I’ve ever looked forward to.

In fact, growing up, I used to dread having to shave because the razors back in my day (yes, I’m going full Grandpa Simpson) would leave me cut up and peppered with bits of tissue to stem the bleeding.

Even shaving creams, foams, and lotions did little to make the experience feel anything other than torturous, and that’s just the face - drift to your pits, or–heaven forbid–below the belt, and you’ll be feeling itchy, sore, or worse for days.

So what of the OneBlade? For one thing, as the name suggests, it’s delightfully simple. You can use it on your boat race, you can use it on your body, and yes, you can use it on your more delicate areas, too.

articles.summary: Join Us, the upcoming open-world co-op game where you can start your very own doomsday cult, just dropped a ton of new gameplay as part of IGN's gamescom programming. You can see more than 11 minutes of exclusive footage in the player below, and get a deeper look into just how the game will work.
body: Earlier this week, developer Wolf Haus games announced that the darkly satirical survival/action cult simulator will be available on PS5 at launch alongside the PC and Xbox Series X/S versions in March 2027. The news of Join Us' PS5 version also featured information on how 4-player co-op will work in both the campaign and free roam.

The live-action trailer featuring former cult members, which you can watch below, introduces us to Jaga, Javier, Ariel, and Elena - who have a "collective experience of over 50 years in their unique societies." This experience involves a cult that is preparing for aliens to arrive on Earth and take us back to the planet we came from, a peaceful cult that focuses on martial arts and self-defense training, and a holistic rejuvenation cult.

In Join Us, players will need to stay vigilant though, as they'll need to keep their recruits happy or they will leave the cult. As the devs put it, "a cult leader without any followers is just a lonely weirdo."
For more from gamescom, be sure to check out everything that was revealed during Opening Night Live.

articles.title: Pokémon TCG Pocket adds a game-changing new kind of card this October
articles.summary: During a Pokémon TCG Pocket panel at the PokémonXP event in San Francisco, The Pokémon Company teased some exciting new types of cards for the mobile game. Namely, dual-type cards will make their way to the popular mobile game soon.
body: Dual-type cards will become a thing in Pokémon TCG Pocket starting in October. The first dual-type card to arrive will be Mega Mewtwo X ex, which is a Psychic/Fighting-type Pokémon. It has 180 HP and a 100+ power Dual Impact ability that reads "If a stadium is in play, this attack does 40 more damage." This was highlighted in the latest trailer for Pokémon TCG Pocket, which also confirmed that ex cards for partner Pokémon Piplup and Fuecoco would arrive in October.

Dual-type Pokémon have been a thing in the video games ever since the first generation, but didn't come to the physical Pokémon Trading Card Game until the mid-2000s. According to Bulbapedia, there have been at least 90 dual-type Pokémon cards released in the decades since.

That made the fact that they were missing from Pokémon TCG Pocket a bit surprising initially, although the digital card game certainly hasn't suffered from a shortage of cards for players to collect. While Mega Mewtwo X ex is the only confirmed dual-type card for Pokémon TCG Pocket right now, a blog post on the Pokémon website confirms that more will follow.

articles.title: EA Officially Reacts Iron Man Leak: "Well, That Didn't Go As Planned"
articles.summary: EA finally acknowledged that some gameplay from Motive Studios' upcoming Iron Man leak, although it isn't ready to show more of the game just yet. "See you when we’re ready," the official X account for the game pledged.
body: Footage of Motive Studios' Iron Man recorded during a test sometime this month made its way online this past week. As Polygon's explainer on the leak broke down, the footage not only showed gameplay of the titular hero flying around in different suits but also confirmed that characters like Pepper Potts, Obadiah Stane, and Madame Masque are in the game.

Considering we haven't seen anything about this Iron Man game since EA first teased the project in 2022, this leak was a big deal. Ultimately, EA determined that this leak was high-profile enough to acknowledge, as it posted on the game's official X account for the first time about the matter.

If you were hoping for an official trailer or first look at gameplay, though, you're out of luck. "Well, that didn't go as planned," the post states. "But now you know, and we've got a lot more to show you. See you when we’re ready."

articles.title: GTA 6's gameplay reveal pulled in 3.97 million peak viewers, overwhelming Twitch and Netflix in the process
articles.summary: Reaction streams to Grand Theft Auto 6 's first gameplay presentation peaked at 3,970,738 viewers across livestreaming platforms, making it the biggest gaming stream of 2026 so far.
body: That's according to new data from Streams Charts, which claims 9,038 streamers covered Rockstar Games ' Netflix reveal, racking up 5,227,798 hours watched.

That puts GTA 6's reveal ahead of Summer Game Fest 2026's 3.81 million peak viewers, as well as June's Nintendo Direct and State of Play broadcasts. Twitch carried the largest share of the audience, accounting for around 44 percent of total hours watched, ahead of YouTube (34.8% percent) and Kick (20.2 percent).
Spanish streamer Juan Alberto "IlloJuan" García led the way with 233,520 peak viewers, a new record for his own channel, ahead of Rubius (191,056) and IShowSpeed (177,887).

The reveal went out at 8pm UK time, but heavy demand caused technical issues on both Netflix and Twitch, with some viewers reportedly locked out for 40-50 minutes. That didn't deter internet hype, though; Streams Charts also tracked more than 100,000 chat messages about the game across the three-hour window it analysed.

articles.title: How 'Coyote vs. ACME' Broke All the Rules of Live-Action Looney Tunes Movies, and Got Away with It
articles.summary: "We really wanted to challenge ourselves to not acknowledge the Looney Tunes as an ensemble of characters," director Dave Green tells Polygon.
body: When Michael Jordan first meets Bugs Bunny in Space Jam, he reacts with star-studded confusion, which is probably how any human being would react to meeting the iconic cartoon rabbit in real life. But when Will Forte meets the beloved Looney Tune in Coyote vs. ACME, he's surprisingly nonplussed. That's because, in the new live-action/animated feature film, the Looney Tunes aren't global icons, they're just regular (cartoon) people living in our world.
Foghorn is a blowhard who has a lot of swagger and arrogance and likes to talk down to people.

Unlike Space Jam and Looney Tunes: Back in Action — or even Who Framed Roger Rabbit — the Looney Tunes characters are not celebrities in Coyote vs. ACME. In those other movies, the Looney Tunes characters play famous versions of themselves that had starred in all those animated shorts from back in the day, but in Coyote vs. ACME, they’re just regular people living in a world populated by both humans and cartoon characters. In that sense, Coyote vs. ACME operates more like a movie-length Looney Tunes animated short than a live-action movie with Looney Tunes characters in it.

articles.title: Gamescom Responds To Rampant Reports Of Theft At The Event
articles.summary: Theft has become a major problem at Gamescom 2026, with at least three indie studios speaking out about the equipment stolen from their event booths. The organization behind the event has acknowledged this matter in an underwhelming X post that did not indicate it would provide indie exhibitors…
body: Reports of theft first emerged when Mimic solo developer Ryan Laley reported that their laptop and other equipment in the expo area near him were stolen. According to Ryan Laley's video explaining the ordeal, the hardware was snatched overnight from an area that is supposed to have restricted access overnight and be monitored by the security team at all times.

In the same raid, Tessera Studios, which was showcasing the game The Zibbo Show, lost personal computers, two laptops, and a Steam Deck, all containing game demos and confidential company information. Additionally, two computers were stolen from indie game publisher iam8bit Presents' booth, risking leaks of its games, Petal Runner and Escape Academy 2.

Ukiyo Studios then chimed in to recall that one of its laptops was taken from a Gamescom booth two years ago. It claims that when it tried to report the theft, event personnel attempted to stop Ukiyo so it wouldn't taint Gamescom and the city of Cologne's public image. Furthermore, Ukiyo says that despite attending dozens of events every year, Gamescom is the only one where it makes sure to lock up the equipment overnight due to inadequate security measures.

articles.title: Squadron 42 delayed to 2027, with Star Citizen dev blaming GTA 6
articles.summary: Cloud Imperium Games has delayed Squadron 42, its long-in-development Star Citizen spin-off, to Q2 2027, with studio boss Chris Roberts arguing the game would be drowned out by GTA 6.
body: The single-player game had been targeting a 2026 release, as Cloud Imperium reaffirmed as recently as late last year. In a new blog post, however, Roberts said launching this autumn would mean going up against Rockstar's blockbuster, something he wasn't willing to risk for a game "that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it".
"At CitizenCon 2024 we announced we would ship in 2026," Roberts wrote (thanks, IGN ).

"Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE. But much like the rest of the industry, there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA6.
"While GTA6 isn't launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage."

articles.title: Rockstar considered having four protagonists in Grand Theft Auto 6, but the studio 'worried about diluting the amount of player time' with each character
articles.summary: One of the most intriguing creative decisions Rockstar made with Grand Theft Auto 6 is reducing the number of playable characters from three to two. Since sequels typically operate on the rule of 'bigger is better', the logical progression would have been to add even more playable characters to the…
body: It turns out that Rockstar did indeed consider this. Speaking to IGN, studio co-head Rod Nelson explained that a GTA with four protagonists was on the table. But Rockstar decided against it due to concerns about spreading the player's attention too thin.

"As the narrative unfolds, we're quite conscious to try and make sure that players have enough time with each character," Nelson explained. "After doing GTA 5, we talked about different ideas of 'Do we have more characters? How do we follow up three characters? Is it four characters now?' But we worried about diluting the amount of player time with each, and therefore player connection with those characters."

This fear of diluting that time spent with each character is also what led Rockstar down the path of two protagonists. "The question became: how do you make players feel like 'I love them both'" Nelson adds. "Chemistry is a notoriously hard thing to do in any sort of entertainment. Either the characters and the actors that embody them have it—or they don't."
points: One of the most intriguing creative decisions Rockstar made with Grand Theft Auto 6 is reducing the number of playable characters from three to two.
Speaking to IGN, studio co-head Rod Nelson explained that a GTA with four protagonists was on the table.
"As the narrative unfolds, we're quite conscious to try and make sure that players have enough time with each character," Nelson explained.
Is it four characters now?' But we worried about diluting the amount of player time with each, and therefore player connection with those characters."

articles.summary: The Pokémon Company International and Aardman have released the first teaser trailer for Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch'd & Pichu, a new stop-motion series set in the Galar region.
body: The video description teases: "Join our unlikely heroes, Sirfetch'd and Pichu, in their gallant quest to protect Pokémon across Galar! While their missions might rarely go as planned, their noble deeds forge their friendship as they step bravely into the unknown. Peril, alliances, rivalries, extraordinary Pokémon, and endless laughs await them."

Pokémon's director of original animation Phil Rynda joined Aardman's Tom Parkinson (director), Nat McKay (creative director, IP development), and James Young (model-making creative lead) on the panel to walk fans through the show's puppets, sets, and production process.
Disney+ was also confirmed as the series' exclusive worldwide streaming home when it arrives in 2027, following the platform's recent addition of Pokémon the Series: The Beginning.

Set across the wilds of Galar, Pokémon Tales follows Sirfetch'd and Pichu on what Pokémon describes as "a gallant quest to help and protect Pokémon across the region", with new Pokémon and location reveals including Obstagoon and the Crown Tundra area, both previously seen in Pokémon Sword and Shield.

articles.title: Hello Neighbor's multiplayer spinoff has been 'temporarily shut down' after a hacker wiped player progression and demanded the game's 'removal from sale across all platforms'
articles.summary: Secret Neighbor, the multiplayer spinoff for the 2017 horror game Hello Neighbor, has been temporarily taken offline following a security breach by a hacker who accessed the game's backend systems and deleted player data.
body: The incident, which occurred last week, involved an individual who obtained credentials with admin access to the game. The hacker then proceeded to wipe player profiles, in-game progression, and other data, while also carrying out what developer Hologryph and publisher tinyBuild described as a "coordinated attack on our server systems and infrastructure" across all platforms.

Hologryph and tinyBuild addressed the situation in a Steam post, (via delistedgames ). They explained that, in addition to the attack, the hacker had "stated they intend to continue targeting the game and its backend systems until the game is removed from sale across all platforms."

According to both companies, no personal data or information had been compromised by the attack. Yet as the incident is ongoing, they have opted to "temporarily shut down the game until we had addressed the breach and closed any vulnerabilities that may have led to the incident."

In its statement, Hologryph and tinyBuild say they have alerted the relevant authorities to the situation. They are also working with PlayFab—the company which provides Secret Neighbour's backend services—in an attempt to recover the data that has been wiped.

videos.title: Fable - Combat Gameplay | PS5 Games
videos.summary: In Fable, you’ll flow seamlessly between melee, ranged, and magical abilities as you come face-to-face with classic creatures and new threats lurking across Albion.
body: Experiment with different loadouts, discover powerful spell combinations, and choose the combat style that feels right for you as you carve your own path through Albion.
Fable launches February 23, 2027. Pre-Order to receive the Pre-Order Content Pack, featuring the questionably heroic Chicken Suit and a collection of charming in-game gifts.
